blocks.prompt: 12 Solve the following trigonometric equation: \(\tan x = \sin 2x\)
blocks.explanation:
Write both sides in \(\sin x\) and \(\cos x\); note that \(\tan x\) needs \(\cos x \ne 0\).
After clearing the fraction, \(\sin x\) is a common factor.
Plan: solve \(\sin x = 0\) and \(\cos^{2}x = \frac{1}{2}\), then check the restriction.
steps:
Given: \(\tan x = \sin 2x\).
To find: principal solutions and general solution.
Method: \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\), \(\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x\); multiply by \(\cos x\) (allowed, since \(\cos x \ne 0\) wherever \(\tan x\) exists) and factorise.

Write in sine and cosine
\[\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x} = 2\sin x\cos x\]
Why: both sides now use the same angle \(x\).

Clear the fraction
\[\sin x = 2\sin x\cos^{2}x\]
\[\sin x - 2\sin x\cos^{2}x = 0\]
\[\sin x\left(1 - 2\cos^{2}x\right) = 0\]
Why: multiply both sides by \(\cos x\); bring all terms to one side and take \(\sin x\) common (do not cancel it).

Two cases
\[\sin x = 0\ \text{ or }\ \cos^{2}x = \dfrac{1}{2}\]
Why: a product is zero only when a factor is zero.

When \(\sin x = 0\)
\[x = 0,\ \pi,\ 2\pi\]
in \([0, 2\pi]\); in general \(x = n\pi\).
Why: sine is zero at every multiple of \(\pi\).

When \(\cos^{2}x = \frac{1}{2}\)
\[\cos x = \pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\]
Reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{4}\).
\[\cos x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}:\ x = \dfrac{\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\]
\[\cos x = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}:\ x = \dfrac{3\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{4}\]
Why: positive cosine in quadrants I, IV; negative in II, III.

Check the restriction
At none of these angles is \(\cos x = 0\), so \(\tan x\) is defined at all of them: no root is rejected.
Why: we multiplied by \(\cos x\), so we must make sure no root has \(\cos x = 0\).

General solution
\[\left\{n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{\pi}{4} + 2n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{3\pi}{4} + 2n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{5\pi}{4} + 2n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{7\pi}{4} + 2n\pi\right\},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\]
Why: union of the families of both cases. The four \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) families are \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) apart, so together they are \(\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{n\pi}{2}\).

Check
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}:\ \tan\dfrac{\pi}{4} = 1,\ \sin\dfrac{\pi}{2} = 1\]
\[x = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}:\ \tan\dfrac{3\pi}{4} = -1,\ \sin\dfrac{3\pi}{2} = -1\]
Why: both sides are equal; at \(x = n\pi\) both sides are 0.
blocks.final_answer: Principal solutions in \([0, 2\pi]\): \(x = 0, \frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{3\pi}{4}, \pi, \frac{5\pi}{4}, \frac{7\pi}{4}, 2\pi\). General solution: \(\left\{n\pi\right\}\) \(\cup\) \(\left\{\frac{\pi}{4} + 2n\pi\right\}\) \(\cup\) \(\left\{\frac{3\pi}{4} + 2n\pi\right\}\) \(\cup\) \(\left\{\frac{5\pi}{4} + 2n\pi\right\}\) \(\cup\) \(\left\{\frac{7\pi}{4} + 2n\pi\right\}\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\). (Shorter form: \(\{n\pi\} \cup \left\{\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{n\pi}{2}\right\}\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\).)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: The textbook prints no answers for Exercise 10.1. Every answer on this page is ours: worked out step by step, checked independently with a computer algebra system (sympy) and compared with a solution book. As in the book's examples, we give the principal solutions in \([0, 2\pi]\) and the general solution as a union of sets.
